note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of known prostate cancer with recent PSA fluctuation and persistent high-grade histology.

The patient is a 65-year-old office administrator, married but living alone, with his spouse as the primary contact. He has a history of prostate cancer diagnosed in August 2023, Gleason 4+3, ISUP grade group 3. His PSA has shown significant variability, rising from 3.4 ng/mL in April 2023 to 8.6 ng/mL in February 2025, with a notable dip to 3.3 ng/mL in August 2024. He is a non-smoker, consumes 15 units of alcohol per week, and swims once weekly. He recently received a flu vaccination from his GP practice nurse. He has no other significant medical history or active medications. He previously declined participation in research trials and wishes this to be respected in any future discussions.

On DRE, a nodular area is palpable in the right mid peripheral zone, consistent with cT2a disease. The remainder of the prostate is smooth and non-tender. General examination is unremarkable, with normal cardiovascular and respiratory findings.

admin: Patient declined research participation previously; respect for AS-related trials.
